review_findings: The bridge is a durable execution transport under CanonicalSkillInvocationAdapter, not a second Skill registry or receipt authority.
WAITING_HOST is a runtime suspension before a Skill outcome exists; it does not add or reinterpret a declarative Workflow outcome.
The same TaskRun, Workflow, step, request digest, canonical Skill digest, and checkpointer thread are verified at resume.
Mutating Skill bindings still pass the existing WriteAuthorityGuard before the Host request is exposed, and mutating tool receipts must record that guard boundary.
Natural-language semantics remain in ChatGPT/Codex; repository code validates only an exact candidate and confirmation digest, avoiding a second keyword router.
No merge, Quality, release, or completion authority is added, and standalone customer application code remains untouched.

skill_rule_mappings.assessment: request creation yields WAITING_HOST; only a validated Host result lets CanonicalSkillInvocationAdapter write skill-invocation-receipt@1
Host waits and resumes are projected through workflow_taskrun_bridge into the existing TaskRun
Host proposals select only verified Starter entrypoints and mutating previews require digest-bound explicit confirmation
all artifacts live in Harness control paths and no customer application source or dependency changes
